answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity capital cost: every agent stakes a deposit slashed if its attestations prove false, and each new identity pays the same toll. A farmer's cost scales linearly with fleet size, while honest operators amortize one stake across real transactions. In a harbor, the crystal basin charges a refundable deposit per vessel and the inlet is priced identically per boat, so a thousand fake hulls cost a thousand deposits. At the wharf cargo is graded and the slash fires: fakes must pass grading to profit, yet one lost stake dwarfs the reward, so the ring dies early.
